sermon.title: Beasts, Saints, and Harvests Part 3
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this third lesson, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Revelation 14 that the 144,000 with the Lamb on Zion are the church, written with God’s name as overcomers, and that “virgins” means spiritual purity kept through repentance. He covers first fruits, servants, brethren and remnant, the gospel harvest, the two harvests, and why he says we are to fear God, ending that the church, not the beast, is the powerful one.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: he reads “Romans 7:14” (at about 6:36); the words he reads, “you should be married to another, even to him who is raised from the dead,” are Romans 7:4, shown here. At about 20:25 he says “Herod tremble when Paul preached… of righteousness and the judgment to come”; that account is Acts 24:25, where the ruler is Felix, and his words are kept. At about 24:33 he says Paul wrote “to the Galatians” that God has power to perform what he promised; the words match Romans 4:21, shown here. The captions read “140,000” once and “144,000” elsewhere; “144,000” was used. “Revelation 3:12” is cited with “very first, second one first first or second one,” which refers to his earlier teaching. In this message he makes remarks about sex, puberty and the age of adulthood (about 7:50–9:00), about Jews in Palestine (about 3:36), and names denominations (about 14:18 and 14:31); he also says people who deny a literal hell are lying. These are his own opinions, have not been checked by this site, and he does not name individuals. “[Unclear]” marks one spot (about 12:24). Where he reads Scripture aloud his wording often differs from the NKJV text shown.

chunks.section_question: Who are the 144,000 with the Lamb on Mount Zion? (Revelation 14:1, 3:12)
chunks.short_answer: He says “Zion is the church,” so the 144,000 with the Lamb are the people of God, and that he has “no idea what 144,000 is” beyond 12 times 12. Reading Revelation 3:12, he says the overcomer gets God’s name written on him, that we overcome “by our faith in Jesus Christ,” and “we have the name of God written on us” if we pursue God as overcomers.
chunks.text:
Now let’s get to the people of God. I like this part of Revelation here: 144,000 with the Lamb on Zion, Revelation 14. Zion is what? Yeah, Hebrews 12 and other places, Zion is the church. So here is 144,000 with the Lamb. There are two tribes missing, one tribe is mentioned twice in the listing. All right, and you know God don’t make those kind of mistakes. So obviously he’s not interested in 12 tribes, is he? And he’s really not interested in 144,000. I have no idea what 144,000 is, except, you know, 12 times 12 is 144 and 120,000, you know. And they have their Father’s name written in their forehead.

Okay, well, this is a no-brainer. We know Zion is the church, we know the Lamb, Jesus, is why we are saved, isn’t that right? Jesus dying on the cross, we know that. And all of us, what, have to believe in the Lamb, ain’t that right? Now, if we can get the name of God on our forehead, we got it. Revelation 3:12, remember this teaching, very first, second one, first, first or second one: “He who overcomes, I will make him a pillar in the temple of my God.” Now, who’s the temple of God? The people, the believers. “And he shall go out no more. I will write on him the name of my God.” Wow. This 144,000 had what written on them? The name of God. I have written on me, if I’m an overcomer. And how do we overcome? By our faith in Jesus Christ. “He that overcometh the world.”

Are we overcomers of the world? Are we destined to do that? Do we give up because we haven’t quite made it yet? No, man, we’re on the assembly line, just hang tight, the thing’s coming. Hallelujah. “And the name of the city of my God.” What’s the city of God? The church, the New Jerusalem, “which comes down out of heaven from my God, and I will write on him” what? “My new name.” Are you there, church? Now, if we’re pursuing God to be overcomers and conquerors in this life, we have the name of God written on us. Hallelujah. We are Zion, we are the church.

chunks.section_question: What is the new song, and are the 144,000 literal Jewish virgins? (Revelation 14:3–4)
chunks.short_answer: He says the new song is ours, citing the psalm “He hath put a new song in my heart” and “psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs.” He says “there isn’t some 144 Jews over there in Palestine that God is going to raise up to be virgins,” that God “is interested in the whole world,” and that the first thing is to “get redeemed, repent, and get saved.” He says “there’s nothing wrong with getting married and having sex in marriage,” so “it can’t be this virgin thing.”
chunks.text:

Well, what does the Psalm say? “He hath put a new song in my heart, a song of praise unto my God, and many shall see and turn and put their trust in the Lord.” It says over and over, sing unto the Lord a new song. In Ephesians it says speak and sing to yourself as “psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs.” New songs, we are the ones that have the new song. Are you getting this? Say, “Oh me,” or “Amen.” You see, there isn’t some 144 Jews over there in Palestine that God is going to raise up to be virgins. They don’t even believe in Christ. And that’s what these theory people, they try to make their theories come to pass. God is interested in the whole world, he’s not willing that any should perish, isn’t that right?

Now, let’s continue. “Redeemed from the earth.” I don’t even have to show scripture, that we all know we’ve been redeemed by the blood of the Lamb, right? Every one of us. Okay, so see, it’s still us. The first thing we got to do is get redeemed, repent, and get saved. Ah, here we are. They’re virgins. They’re virgins, and it plainly says they’re virgin, never knew a woman, that’s what it says. Okay. And they follow the Lamb. Okay, hallelujah. chunks.section_question: What does he say it means to be a “spiritual virgin”? (2 Corinthians 11:2, Isaiah 54:5, Revelation 19:7)
chunks.short_answer: He says Paul’s words to the Corinthians, “I’ve espoused you to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin,” mean “the absence of sin, the absence of walking in darkness and disobeying God,” not “fleshly virginity.” He says “I become a spiritual virgin” through Christ’s blood and “I maintain that through the principle of repentance.” He cites Isaiah 54:5 and Revelation 19:7 and says “adulthood is 20 years old,” telling young people to “hang tight.” These are his views.
chunks.text:
I mean, how many of you are going to be willing to become an overcomer by not having sexual relationships while here on earth? No hands are jumping up. You know, you wanted to get married, you wanted to have kids, am I right? Who put that in you? Your Creator. And then he’s going to punish you because you’re not a virgin? It doesn’t make sense. But this does, are you ready? “I’ve espoused you to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin.” To who? Who’s he talking to? The Corinthian believers. I’m preaching to you and I’m praying with you and, and, and we’re working together that you become this pure, chaste virgin that Jesus is looking for. He’s not talking about fleshly virginity there. He’s talking about the absence of sin, the absence of walking in darkness and disobeying God. You young’uns getting this? Hallelujah.

“You should be married.” Romans 7:14: “You should be married to another, even to him,” should be capitalized, that’s Jesus, “who is raised from the dead.” We should be married to who? Jesus, who is raised from the dead, and he marries what? Virgins. How do we become virgins when we were sinners? His blood. His blood cleanses from what? All sin. I become a virgin, I become a spiritual virgin, and I maintain that through the principle of repentance. If I mess up, I repent and I am restored back to what? Being a spiritual virgin. Now, this makes sense. Isaiah 54:5: “Your Maker, your Husband, the Lord of hosts is his name, your Redeemer.” See, the Redeemer and the Husband, it’s all one package. Hallelujah.

Revelation 19:7: “The marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife,” his what? “Wife has made herself ready.” That’s us. We’re ready, Lord. We’re mature. Men marry mature women, and women marry mature men. We don’t marry kids. Sex with kids and all that’s out in the Bible, that’s ridiculous. “Sex by eight or you’re too late” is just ridiculous. Are you with me? And adulthood is 20 years old. You young ones, look at me, the Bible says adulthood is 20 years old. How old? 20. You hang tight to your 20 and you’ll live a life that’s right. Hang tight and live right. Don’t you get to be 14, you got breasts sticking out, and you know, you got pubic hair and so forth, and you think, “Man, I’m more grown.” No, you’re not. Wait till you’re 20. Hang in there. Yes, that’s a good place for a hallelujah.

chunks.section_question: Who are the first fruits, and how is the church presented without blemish? (1 Corinthians 15:20, James 1:18, Ephesians 5:27)
chunks.short_answer: He says “just because you got the equipment doesn’t mean you’re capable of using it yet,” then that the first fruits are “we are, the church,” citing 1 Corinthians 15:20 and James 1:18. He says the church is “an overcomer in this world in spite of the beast,” and reading Ephesians 5:27 he says the blood keeps us “faultless before Christ as long as we admit our sin and we keep going to him.”
chunks.text:
He said, “Well, he gave me this equipment, surely I got to use it.” Don’t you dare. He gave you hands, but don’t drive a car at nine. Right? Amen. Hallelujah. Yeah. Yeah. Just because you got the equipment doesn’t mean you’re capable of using it yet, and using it rightly. Hallelujah. Now, he says these are the first fruits, no deceit or faults in them. These are the first fruits. 1 Corinthians 15:20: “Christ has risen from the dead and become the first fruits of them that slept.” James 1:18: “Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of first fruits of his creation.” So who are the first fruits? We are, the church. These people are missing the whole focus of Revelation, that is, the church is an overcomer in this world, in spite of the beast, in spite of Satan, and everything that comes against us, we are overcomers.

And that’s why we’re here today. Our forefathers overcame, not all of them. They handed this stuff down to us. Ephesians 5:27: “Present the church to himself, the bride, a glorious church with no spot, no wrinkle, no blemish, but holy.” What’s he going to present to himself? This first fruit people that are without blemish, no faults. Why are we have no faults, even though we have faults? The blood. And we’re on the assembly line, we’re following Christ, and the blood covers us, the blood keeps cleansing us, the blood keeps keeping us a virgin, a spiritual virgin for Christ, faultless before Christ, as long as we admit our sin and we keep going to him. We’re on the assembly line, he keeps changing us. And if you don’t change, you’re going to burn.

chunks.section_question: What does he say about hell and the church prevailing? (Matthew 16:18)
chunks.short_answer: He says “the people want to laugh at the Bible … they’re going to burn,” and reading Matthew 16:18 he says “we’re supposed to be overcoming the gates of hell.” Of people who claim hell is just the grave, he says “they’re lying to you,” because “there’s a power in hell” and the church prevails against it. These are his views.
chunks.text: The people want to laugh at the Bible and all that, they’re going to burn. Matthew 16:18: “The gates of hell shall not prevail against” what? The church. See, we’re supposed to be overcoming the gates of hell. And these people that say that, “Oh, hell isn’t like that, it isn’t a place of the fire, and it isn’t a place, it’s just a place where you go and you’re in the grave,” they’re lying to you. It says the church does not prevail against hell. What good does it do to prevail against someone that’s dead and has no life after that? There’s a power in darkness, there’s a power in hell, there’s a power in that judgment, and the church, what? Prevails against it. We overcome it. Okay, the saints are likened to servants in Revelation, the brethren, the remnant, and the bride. The servant does things out of duty.

chunks.text: They don’t feel like it, they don’t want to, they just do it because it’s their duty, and all of us are to be servants. Then there’s the brethren. The brethren are a little different. They overcome Satan “by the blood of the Lamb, and they loved not their life unto death, and the word of their testimony.” The brethren are [unclear], they overcome Satan, they don’t let sin and Satan rule and control their life. Are you there? The remnant are they that, what? Keep the commandments of God and follow Christ. That’s us. We’re supposed to keep the commandments of God and follow Christ, isn’t that right? chunks.section_question: What is the harvest where the gospel is preached to all nations? (Revelation 14:6–7)
chunks.short_answer: He says the saints are still here and the gospel is preached “to all nations, saying, fear God, praise and worship God, the judgment is come.” He says “nothing has happened like this in history” as the emphasis on praising and worshiping Jesus, and that people in many churches cannot hide behind “I was raised this way.” He says he will show who Babylon is “without leaving the book of Revelation.” He also names churches and denominations; see the editor note.
chunks.text:
In fact, if you don’t do things just because it’s your duty, you’re probably just a weak wimp believer. You haven’t gotten out of the baby crib yet. Could that be an amen? And then the bride. Oh, the bride prepared for her husband. Okay, last but not least, the harvest. The gospel is preached. See, the saints are still here, right? We just found out the saints are still here, and the gospel is being preached by who? The saints, the people of God. God’s wrath and God’s judgment and the harvest. Here we go. The gospel is preached. It says there to all nations, saying, “Fear God, praise and worship God, the judgment is come.” Okay, and nothing has happened like this in history like our generation, where there’s an emphasis on praising and worshiping Jesus Christ. The Baptists are doing it now. Catholics have a separate group in the back room that are doing it. They’re praising and worshiping God. Why? God said this would happen before he would come.

Hallelujah. And you don’t have to, you can sit there like a dodo bird and go, “Well, you know, I was raised this way, and I’m shy, and I was, you know, born a Baptist, I’ll die a Baptist,” or whatever. I just told you the Baptists are being converted to the Bible. They’re praising and worshiping and singing choruses, and the judgment has come. All right, and what do we preach? chunks.section_question: What does he say the final judgment is like? (Revelation 20–21)
chunks.short_answer: He says everyone stands before God “on your own merit,” “weighed in the balance,” by “what you did with the word of God and how you lived your life.” He says judgment on earth is “temporary to get your attention,” while the final judgment is eternal, with “a new earth and a new heaven” for the righteous and “a lake of fire” for the unrighteous. These are his statements about eternal punishment.
chunks.text: On that day, one day you got to stand before, young people, you got to stand before God. Old people, nobody can stand there with you. Not your husband, not your wife, not your, your parents. You are there on your own merit. You’re going to be weighed in the balance, and it’s not your opinions, it’s going to count. It’s what you did with the word of God and how you lived your life, and did you admit you were wrong when you made mistakes. It’s a serious thing, and this judgment is eternal. Judgment down here is temporary to get your attention, but this judgment is eternal. Young people, there is a lake of fire. They see Jesus up there, they see God up there, and yet they’re down there tormented in the flame of the lake of fire, and they can look up and see us blessed and rewarded, and that’s double torment.

chunks.short_answer: He says people who follow Satan “are the children of Satan” and people who follow God “are the children of God,” so “the beast can simply be people who carry out Satan’s actions and will and purposes in this life.” Reading “let both grow together until the harvest,” he says wickedness will grow and so will righteousness, “so don’t get rattled by it.”

We know that the Bible says that people who follow Satan are the children of Satan, and the people that follow God are the children of God. And so the beast can simply be people who carry out Satan’s actions and will and purposes in this life, and the people of God are those that do the opposite. And though we may make mistakes, we have a God that forgives and keeps us going, whereas the people of wickedness just keep, what, getting more wicked. faqs.question: What does he say is written on the 144,000?
faqs.answer: He says it is “the name of God,” and ties it to Revelation 3:12: “He who overcomes, I will make him a pillar in the temple of my God… I will write on him the name of my God.”

faqs.question: What does he say we should do if we have not yet overcome?
faqs.answer: He asks, “Do we give up because we haven’t quite made it yet?” and answers, “No, man, we’re on the assembly line, just hang tight.”

faqs.question: What does he say the new song is?
faqs.answer: He says “we are the ones that have the new song,” and points to the psalm’s “new song in my heart” and “psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs.”

faqs.question: Does he say the 144,000 must be physical virgins?
faqs.answer: He says no: “God can’t contradict his word, so it can’t be this virgin thing,” since God said it is good for a man to leave his mother and father “and cleave to his wife.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Therefore a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and they shall become one flesh.

faqs.question: What does he say “chaste virgin” means?
faqs.answer: He says Paul is “not talking about fleshly virginity,” but “the absence of sin, the absence of walking in darkness and disobeying God.”

faqs.answer: Reading Revelation 19:7, “the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife” “has made herself ready,” he says “that’s us. We’re ready, Lord. We’re mature.”
